question: Your support agent calls escalate_to_human for a billing dispute after it confirms a duplicate charge that exceeds its refund limit. The human agents who receive escalations cannot see the conversation transcript. They report that they spend several minutes re-asking customers for details. Which two changes best address this problem?

options.text: Keep each escalation note to one short free-form sentence, so the human agent can read it quickly between calls.
options.reason: A short free-form note leaves out the structured fields the guide names, such as customer ID, root cause, refund amount and recommended action.

options.text: Define the escalate_to_human input schema with required fields for customer ID, root cause, refund amount, and recommended action.
options.reason: Required schema fields make every handoff carry the customer ID, root cause, refund amount and recommended action, so the human agent can act without the transcript.

options.text: Pass only the customer ID, so the human agent can look up the orders and work out the root cause from backend records.
options.reason: The guide says a handoff should include root cause, refund amount and recommended action, so the human agent should not have to repeat the investigation.

options.text: Have the agent tell the customer to restate the full problem to the human agent after the transfer completes.
options.reason: This shifts the work back to the customer and gives no structured handoff summary, which the guide requires when the human agent lacks the transcript.

options.text: Have the agent compile a structured summary of its findings and its recommended next step before it calls escalate_to_human.
options.reason: The guide calls for structured handoff summaries with root cause analysis and recommended actions when the human agent lacks the transcript.
